’An assassin from the Dawn Minion and he was told to abduct Mom? I’m sure they were probably kargeking—cough—targeting me. But who could be behind it? The king? Or someone else?’ Vritra wondered. He knew a low level assassin wouldn’t know anything, so he decided not to waste his time on useless things and asked the final question.
"Where is your base?"
"U- Under... cough cough... khe biggesk black markek, away from... cough cough... khe capikal..." the assassin finished this, barely breathing.

"Alright, we are done with him. Throw him down." Vritra ordered as the assassin’s dead and despaired eyes opened wide, but before he could speak, the dark knight let go of his neck as the frail body fell to the ground.
The two watched as the assassin fell to the empty street and died instantly. Vritra looked at the dark knight and ordered:

"I am going to the base of the Dawn Minion. By the time I return, make sure to collect all the guards who had ignored the existence of these assassins. No matter where they are or what they are doing, just abduct them all and bring them to the entrance of the forest towards the labyrinth."
"I understand, master." The dark knight bowed and then faded away, disappearing from sight instantly.
"Bob, go and stay near my mother. Kill anyone if they try to harm her." Vritra ordered, as another shadow flew into the distance at an even faster speed.
Now Vanessa would be much more safe, and he could take his sweet time wiping out the entire Dawn Minion.

"Now, it’s time to head to the biggest black market. From this day forth, the Dawn Minion will cease to exist in this world." Vritra mumbled and flew away. But since he didn’t know the exact location, he had to ask for directions a few times before he was able to arrive at his destination.

While flying there, Vritra felt that now there was a strong need for his soul wraiths to grow. Dark knight, Hellmancer and the chimera, all of them needed to grow stronger and at least become myriad soul wraiths.
And he had a plan for that.

Soon Vritra found himself standing in a bustling market. Though most of the people walking on the streets here didn’t look like high class people, most of them looked around to find new targets for stealing or scamming.

Vritra walked calmly on the street while looking around. He had a naïve look on his face that attracted the attention of dozens of people. It wasn’t long before a shady looking man approached him with a smile, while rubbing his palms together.

"Oh young lord, tell me, are you looking for something? I am the best man here to buy information from. Just say the name and you will get it if it exists. Just tell me what it is you seek and I will make it available," said the shady guy, who was rather slim.

Vritra looked left and right, then he took a step closer to the shady guy and spoke in a low voice, as if he was about to speak some secret. His actions greatly intrigued the shady guy, who thought he had caught a big fish.
"Your mother. Is she available?" Vritra asked in all seriousness, even his face was dripping with solemnness.
"..." The shady guy was taken aback. For a few seconds, he stared at Vritra in confusion, then his face twisted in rage. He almost attacked Vritra but held back, speaking through gritted teeth.
"Young lord, let’s not joke around here. Reckless words might cost you your life."
"Hey, I was just joking. Anyway, I want to kill someone and I heard that the Dawn Minion is here. Can you tell me how can I—" Vritra began to speak, maintaining a small smile.
But before he could finish, the slim shady guy hushed him as he looked around carefully before muttering in a low voice.
"Shhh! Don’t you know? You can’t speak out that name or you won’t even know how you’ll die."
"Oh, the Dawn Minion is that dangerous?" Vritra asked, matching his low tone.

"Hah, dangerous? It seems you are really naïve. You don’t even know anything about them? Come to this side. A newbie like you would get killed instantly." The shady guy gestured for Vritra to follow and walked to a rather empty corner of the street.

"Cough... it isn’t easy to find the Dawn Minion, but you’ve come to the right person. I can bring you up to them and you can give your bounty there." After a pause, he added, "Just give me, you know, my cut for bringing you there."
Vritra didn’t want to linger around, so he asked, "How much?"
"Eighty silver coins." The guy replied, gazing at Vritra’s face deeply to see his reaction.
"Whoa, that much? How can I have so much?" he pretended, since he didn’t want another group of greedy men to follow him.
"Tch, fine, just give me ten silver coins and I will bring you there." The shady guy huffed and said it as if making a great loss.
"I can only give you eight. I need some for the bounty." Vritra rummaged through his pocket and took out a few coins from his inventory.
"Sigh... fine, you are a lucky brat that I am in a great mood today. Let’s go," said the shady guy and began to lead Vritra away.
"How many members does it have?" Vritra asked while following behind silently.
"Hmm... should be more than three hundred or maybe four hundred. I’m not sure." The other man replied lazily.
"Oh, and how strong is the leader?" Vritra asked another question, irritating him.

"Tsk. You just paid 8 coins and even want all the intel? Damn it, I’ll make a loss this time. The leader is nearly as strong as the Golden Knight—the one who died recently, you know." The shady guy replied, and entered a rather shabby hotel. Then he sat at the window side table and hit the bell on the table. Then he whispered in a low voice, "He is called Dawn."
"I heard that this group is related to the king himself. Is that true?" Vritra asked.
"Shhh! You can’t say that out loud. Sigh... how can you be so stupid? That is a taboo topic." Shaking his head, he changed the topic.
"Just get your task done and don’t get involved in useless matters. Ahem, waiter, come here." He shouted when no one approached despite ringing the bell.
"Tch! What do you want? Pay the money before you order. I can’t have beggars dining here," a fat man with a big mole on his nose walked towards them. He was sweating heavily.
He first looked at the shady guy and spoke, then glanced at Vritra and was surprised to see someone rich like that in his humble—or rather, shitty—hotel.

sentences.text: The assassin shook his head weakly and continued: "An a- assassin... ughh... cough... from khe Dawn Minion.
I... ughh... was kold... cough cough... ko abduck... huff... khak woman.
I don’k know anykhing else." The assassin spoke.
There were more disturbances than information itself.
But Vritra understood it all.
’An assassin from the Dawn Minion and he was told to abduct Mom?
I’m sure they were probably kargeking—cough—targeting me.
But who could be behind it?
The king?
Or someone else?’ Vritra wondered.
He knew a low level assassin wouldn’t know anything, so he decided not to waste his time on useless things and asked the final question.
"Where is your base?"
"U- Under... cough cough... khe biggesk black markek, away from... cough cough... khe capikal..." the assassin finished this, barely breathing.
"Alright, we are done with him.
Throw him down." Vritra ordered as the assassin’s dead and despaired eyes opened wide, but before he could speak, the dark knight let go of his neck as the frail body fell to the ground.
The two watched as the assassin fell to the empty street and died instantly.
Vritra looked at the dark knight and ordered:
"I am going to the base of the Dawn Minion.
By the time I return, make sure to collect all the guards who had ignored the existence of these assassins.
No matter where they are or what they are doing, just abduct them all and bring them to the entrance of the forest towards the labyrinth."
"I understand, master." The dark knight bowed and then faded away, disappearing from sight instantly.
"Bob, go and stay near my mother.
Kill anyone if they try to harm her." Vritra ordered, as another shadow flew into the distance at an even faster speed.
Now Vanessa would be much more safe, and he could take his sweet time wiping out the entire Dawn Minion.
"Now, it’s time to head to the biggest black market.
From this day forth, the Dawn Minion will cease to exist in this world." Vritra mumbled and flew away.
But since he didn’t know the exact location, he had to ask for directions a few times before he was able to arrive at his destination.
While flying there, Vritra felt that now there was a strong need for his soul wraiths to grow.
Dark knight, Hellmancer and the chimera, all of them needed to grow stronger and at least become myriad soul wraiths.
And he had a plan for that.
Soon Vritra found himself standing in a bustling market.
Though most of the people walking on the streets here didn’t look like high class people, most of them looked around to find new targets for stealing or scamming.
Vritra walked calmly on the street while looking around.
He had a naïve look on his face that attracted the attention of dozens of people.
It wasn’t long before a shady looking man approached him with a smile, while rubbing his palms together.
"Oh young lord, tell me, are you looking for something?
I am the best man here to buy information from.
Just say the name and you will get it if it exists.
Just tell me what it is you seek and I will make it available," said the shady guy, who was rather slim.
Vritra looked left and right, then he took a step closer to the shady guy and spoke in a low voice, as if he was about to speak some secret.
His actions greatly intrigued the shady guy, who thought he had caught a big fish.
"Your mother.
Is she available?" Vritra asked in all seriousness, even his face was dripping with solemnness.
"..." The shady guy was taken aback.

He almost attacked Vritra but held back, speaking through gritted teeth.
"Young lord, let’s not joke around here.
Reckless words might cost you your life."
"Hey, I was just joking.
Anyway, I want to kill someone and I heard that the Dawn Minion is here.
Can you tell me how can I—" Vritra began to speak, maintaining a small smile.
But before he could finish, the slim shady guy hushed him as he looked around carefully before muttering in a low voice.
"Shhh!
Don’t you know?
You can’t speak out that name or you won’t even know how you’ll die."
"Oh, the Dawn Minion is that dangerous?" Vritra asked, matching his low tone.
"Hah, dangerous?
It seems you are really naïve.
You don’t even know anything about them?
Come to this side.
A newbie like you would get killed instantly." The shady guy gestured for Vritra to follow and walked to a rather empty corner of the street.

I can bring you up to them and you can give your bounty there." After a pause, he added, "Just give me, you know, my cut for bringing you there."
Vritra didn’t want to linger around, so he asked, "How much?"

"Whoa, that much?

chapters.title: Chapter 118: Big Bounty
paragraphs: "Ahem. What do you want to order, sirs?" His attitude changed immediately.
"Two chickens, one horse, two moon wine and one boar," the shady guy said casually.
The fat man’s attitude changed instantly. He wrinkled his nose and asked, "Anything to pack?"
"No, nothing. Just three kids and two pigs. That will be all for now," the shady guy said with a knowing smile.
The fat man nodded his head as the fat in his cheeks jiggled, then he pointed toward a door that led to the kitchen before speaking, "Gentlemen, please follow me."

Vritra and the shady guy stood up and walked towards the kitchen. Then they walked out from the back of the shop and continued to follow the fat man. Soon, he stopped in front of a small metallic door with a window beside it that was closed, and a few words were written on it:
—Get lost or get a toast, happy deals—
The fat guy knocked on the window over five times and then began to whisper some code. After a brief exchange, the door opened as a masked man walked out in a black outfit. He was at level 278.
’Hmm, not bad. Killing them all would increase Hellmancer’s level quite a bit,’ Vritra thought. He wasn’t going to let even a single one escape.
"You can enter," the masked man pointed at Vritra and gestured, while the two others instantly began to walk away.

"Be careful inside. After giving your mission, just leave this place as soon as you can. A naïve person might end up in trouble," the shady guy sighed before walking away from there. For some reason, he was a bit worried, though he didn’t know that his worries were misplaced.

Vritra nodded and walked through the metallic door, following behind the masked man. There must be quite a lot of assassins currently on missions, and Vritra didn’t want to let a single person from this organisation live—even if most members weren’t involved in the previous night’s attack.

Vritra walked through the compact path, then climbed down a couple of floors. He could already sense the presence of hundreds of men; he was sure there should be at least six hundred currently present here.

As they arrived on the 2nd underground floor, he saw a large hall. Lots of people filled the entire space— some were standing and chatting, some were sitting and eating. There were lots of rooms and all kinds of shops and items.

It was a bit hard to imagine that such a large place was built beneath the black market. As Vritra walked, all the gazes were drawn toward him. They were all assassins, so the air was thick with bloodlust.
{Sin Point Gained: Watched +224}

Vritra’s steps halted suddenly. To others, it looked like he was afraid, so they scoffed and went back to their activities. But Vritra had the instant urge to start slaughtering all these rats— he held back his killing intent.

"Go there and give your money and target’s details, and leave through the same way. If you linger around, you might never make it out of here," the masked man laughed sinisterly and walked back, climbing up the stairs.
Vritra looked around for a few seconds, then walked to the man who was busy writing down the missions. Vritra paused in front of one of them and cleared his throat.
"Oh, wait a second, let me finish this." The man, who barely knew how to hold the pen, wrote messy letters on the paper and, after a couple of minutes, finally glanced up at Vritra.
"A rich boy, huh? Tell me who you want to kill— his strength. The more details you share, the better," said the illiterate man.
"...I want to hire the entire Dawn Minion organization. Every single assassin you have, to kill just one person," Vritra said, and the other man began to write it down.
"Alright, the entire organization, and how strong is that man exactly— wait, what the—" but he suddenly paused as those words finally sank into his thick skull.
But Vritra continued seriously, "I’m not sure exactly how strong he is. His name is Vritra Arclis and he stays in the castle—"
But he was interrupted by the illiterate man, who slammed the book on the table and looked angrily at Vritra.
"Are you messing with me? Get the fuck out of here if you don’t want to die. Hah, what shitty luck. Why is everyone like that today?"

"I’m serious. Tell me how much money I need to pay—everyone, including the leader—to complete this mission for me?" Vritra said, waving his hand in the air and releasing a bit of his aura, which seemed to calm the illiterate man a bit.
"Haa... just leave. Things don’t work like that here. You won’t be able to afford the entire Dawn Minion. Leave before someone hears you speak," he said, shaking his head.

"Just tell me how much I need to pay. I’ve got a lot of money." Vritra said, as he tapped on the table and a large pile of gold instantly filled the entire table, making the surroundings shine in yellow.
A lot of sin points came pouring.

So much gold instantly attracted the attention of everyone around, but Vritra put it away instantly. It was the money he had received from Diana. She had given him a lot of money and valuables happily as a gift— she was quite happy when he took it.
"This is just a little. I have much more. So just gather everyone in the Dawn Minion and I will pay whatever price you need," Vritra said, a faint pinkish light flashing in his eyes.
[Natural Hypnosis Activated.]

"Y- Yes sir, but I can’t d-decide something of this calibre on my own. Please give me a little time to discuss this with the upper levels." The illiterate man stood up in haste, his eyes still wide. He felt a little greedy—like most of the other men present there.

"Sure. But each and every single member of your organisation should be present— even your leader— as fast as possible. Otherwise, I will just leave." Vritra reminded him, as the illiterate man ran away in haste and shouted "yes!" from the distance.
{Sin Point Gained: Got Threatened +254}
The people in the surroundings were very tempted to just kill him and take all his money, but it seemed he was some important customer, so none of them dared to act.
Vritra didn’t have to wait for long, as the illiterate man brought someone dressed in black, with a strong aura surrounding him.
He was near level 600 and should be one of the strongest people under the leader in the entire organisation. Vritra wasted no time and instantly got to the topic.
"How much do you need for me to hire your entire organisation?"
"We can’t talk here. Follow me." The tall man, over seven feet in height, spoke before turning and walking away.
Vritra clicked his tongue. He just wanted to slaughter them all, but it seemed to be taking too much time— so he decided to use a different approach.

chapters.title: Chapter 119: Sponge
paragraphs: Vritra and the tall assassin walked into an exquisite office. It was clean and luxurious, unlike the large hall they had just been in. After entering, the tall man sat on a big, comfortable chair and gestured for Vritra to sit in front of him.
"Now, tell me, why do you want to hire the entire Dawn Minion?" the tall assassin asked.
"Before we go to that topic, I’m curious about a few things." Vritra raised two of his fingers and sat calmly.

"...Ask away." The tall man frowned slightly under his mask and nodded. Since Vritra was an important customer, he needed to pamper him a bit, and it was normal to have some doubts if the mission was this big.
"How many members do you have in your organization?" Vritra asked, putting down one finger.
"More than a thousand," the tall man replied vaguely.

"And in case of emergency, how do you gather every single member of the Dawn Minion? Like from the top leader to the very last member? Is there a way to call them in a short time?" Vritra asked, putting down the other finger.

"..." The tall man narrowed his eyes for a moment, but sensing Vritra’s weak aura, he didn’t think for a moment that he could be attacked. And since this information wasn’t a top secret, he nodded and replied, "Yes, there is a way. We have a signal that could only be used in case of maximum danger, which will summon every assassin of the Dawn Minion, even the leader."
"Whoa, can I see it? I mean, the object you use to send such a signal?" Vritra asked, slightly leaning forward and showing intrigue.
"..." The tall man was about to refuse, but Vritra instantly added:
"If you show it to me, I will add an extra thirty percent to whatever fee we agree on—and give you a big secret about the Nine Pacts and Golden Moon."

Now he was tempted. The tall man began to ponder while holding his chin. If it was just showing him, then it should be fine, right? Not to mention the large amount of extra money—that kind of information could be very helpful in their business.
"Sigh, fine. But you can’t tell anyone ever about this, alright?" he asked, then pulled out a blue cube with three or so centimeters of side length.

"Yes, definitely. I’m just very curious." Vritra looked at the cube with interest. He had seen one when he had married Yasmine, in that dream. The demon lord had pulled a cube and used Demon God’s energy from it.
He decided to ask Yasmine about it later on.

After a slight hesitation, the tall man pulled out a fist sized spherical glass ball from the cube. The sphere seemed to be filled with a bright white light— it looked like nothing more than a decorative item.
"Wow, that looks pretty. Is this really the tool to summon everyone?" Vritra asked, gazing at the glass ball.

"Yes. By crushing this, I can send the danger signal to everyone. This is for the highest threat level signal," the tall man replied in a flat tone. With the way he was holding it, the sphere indeed seemed quite important.
"Oh, I have something like that too," Vritra said just as the tall man was about to put the ball away. He halted and looked at this pretty boy curiously.
Without wasting a moment, Vritra took out a similar sized sphere— except it was dark in color with fog rising around its body, and it had a metallic surface.
"What is tha—" the tall man was about to speak, but Vritra interrupted him.
"See for yourself." After speaking, he lazily threw the ball at the tall man, who was a bit surprised at first but then stretched his hand to catch it.
WHOOSH
All of a sudden, just mid motion, the speed of the dark metallic ball increased exponentially and it curved in the air.
CRACK

First, it tore through the right hand that was holding the glass sphere, breaking it at the same time. Then the metallic sphere—or rather Bobby—pierced through his throat and came out the back of his neck. All of it happened way too fast.
{Sin Point Gained: Paralyzed +1}
"Ughhhh COUGH COUGH"

The tall man was frozen for a moment, his mind unable to understand the sudden changes. Then blood flooded out of his throat as he coughed violently and tightly held his throat, his eyes widening in shock and fear.
At the same time, the white light from the broken sphere was released—and it just vanished.
In the next moment, the token that was lying inside the tall man’s clothes began to buzz heavily and glow.
"I don’t think that would be enough to kill him. Bobby, continue," Vritra commanded, waving away the thin wall of dust that had appeared in front of him to block off the blood.
"Forbid: Agility."
[Forbidden Activated.]
After speaking, he stood up and began to walk around the office, casually looking at the things there.
The tall man held his throat tightly and could do nothing else. It was like his body was moving extremely slowly—just waving his arm would take a minute or more.
Light flashed in his eyes and that dangerous ball appeared once again. It moved way too fast. In an instant, Bobby moved back and forth, piercing through the tall man’s body again and again.
WHOOSH WHOOSH WHOOSH
Blood kept flowing out of his body, as within moments his body was riddled with dozens of holes. He had truly been turned into a sponge.
"Oh, they are fast. So many of them are already here." Vritra stretched his arms and neck, then took out the Axes of Chaos. He wouldn’t feel satisfied if Bobby was the only one to have all the fun.
"Let’s start the slaughter—only this time, with humans." Vritra’s smile stretched across his face, a dense killing intent bursting out of his body.
Already, hundreds of people were about to charge into the office. It seemed the signal even showed the exact location where it was activated.
By now, Bobby was done with its work. It floated around Vritra, ready to act whenever it was ordered. But with his armor—who could harm Vritra in this place?
"Killllll!! The signal came from the 2nd office! Charge, everyone!!"
"The highest level threat! Brothers, Dawn Minion is facing a crisis—let’s join hands and get rid of the danger together!"
Such shouts rang out from the outside. Vritra glanced back at the tall man who was on the verge of death, gaping holes present all over his body.

He was about to die. Vritra called out Hellmancer and ordered it to collect the souls of all the people. Then he didn’t wait for the attackers as he walked toward the doors. He casually hit the doors with the hammer side of his axe, and they exploded into pieces.
Then he walked out—in front of an army of more than five hundred men.
Their levels ranged from above 100 to over 500, while more of them kept charging in from the outside.
{Sin Point Gained: Watched +537}
{Sin Point Gained: Locked on +538}
{Sin Point Gained: Surprised +541}

All of a sudden, just mid motion, the speed of the dark metallic ball increased exponentially and it curved in the air.
CRACK
First, it tore through the right hand that was holding the glass sphere, breaking it at the same time.
Then the metallic sphere—or rather Bobby—pierced through his throat and came out the back of his neck.
All of it happened way too fast.
{Sin Point Gained: Paralyzed +1}
"Ughhhh COUGH COUGH"
The tall man was frozen for a moment, his mind unable to understand the sudden changes.
Then blood flooded out of his throat as he coughed violently and tightly held his throat, his eyes widening in shock and fear.
At the same time, the white light from the broken sphere was released—and it just vanished.
In the next moment, the token that was lying inside the tall man’s clothes began to buzz heavily and glow.
"I don’t think that would be enough to kill him.
Bobby, continue," Vritra commanded, waving away the thin wall of dust that had appeared in front of him to block off the blood.
"Forbid: Agility."
[Forbidden Activated.]
After speaking, he stood up and began to walk around the office, casually looking at the things there.
The tall man held his throat tightly and could do nothing else.
It was like his body was moving extremely slowly—just waving his arm would take a minute or more.
Light flashed in his eyes and that dangerous ball appeared once again.
It moved way too fast.
In an instant, Bobby moved back and forth, piercing through the tall man’s body again and again.
WHOOSH WHOOSH WHOOSH
Blood kept flowing out of his body, as within moments his body was riddled with dozens of holes.
He had truly been turned into a sponge.
"Oh, they are fast.
So many of them are already here." Vritra stretched his arms and neck, then took out the Axes of Chaos.
He wouldn’t feel satisfied if Bobby was the only one to have all the fun.
"Let’s start the slaughter—only this time, with humans." Vritra’s smile stretched across his face, a dense killing intent bursting out of his body.
Already, hundreds of people were about to charge into the office.
It seemed the signal even showed the exact location where it was activated.
By now, Bobby was done with its work.
It floated around Vritra, ready to act whenever it was ordered.
But with his armor—who could harm Vritra in this place?
"Killllll!!
The signal came from the 2nd office!
Charge, everyone!!"
"The highest level threat!
Brothers, Dawn Minion is facing a crisis—let’s join hands and get rid of the danger together!"
Such shouts rang out from the outside.
Vritra glanced back at the tall man who was on the verge of death, gaping holes present all over his body.
He was about to die.
Vritra called out Hellmancer and ordered it to collect the souls of all the people.
Then he didn’t wait for the attackers as he walked toward the doors.
He casually hit the doors with the hammer side of his axe, and they exploded into pieces.
Then he walked out—in front of an army of more than five hundred men.
Their levels ranged from above 100 to over 500, while more of them kept charging in from the outside.
{Sin Point Gained: Watched +537}
{Sin Point Gained: Locked on +538}
{Sin Point Gained: Surprised +541}

chapters.title: Chapter 120: Tiny Devils
paragraphs: A bloody aura exploded around Vritra, expanding dangerously with each step he took forward. Holding the two heavy and large axes, with thick bloody mist around him; just the sight alone made most of the assassins tremble.
STEP
STEP

The killing intent expanded over a vast area, completely engulfing the entire black market. Most of the people fainted under the suffocating pressure. Vritra allowed his aura to completely devour everything.
[Sin Point Gained: Aggravated +18]
"H- He is...? Isn’t he the one that came just now to hire an assassin?"
"No, he wanted to hire the entire Dawn Minion. He’s the intruder? Just him? Was the highest threat level... this brat?"
Everyone was shocked, but as they sensed his killing intent—one that even astonished the assassins—they could no longer take him lightly.
"Why are you here? Are there more here with you? Tell us everything or you will be killed—" one of the assassins, whose level was close to 400, stepped forward and said with narrowed eyes.
But Vritra wasted no time. His madness had already reached its peak, and he had held back for too long.
He took one step forward as his figure blurred. In the next second, Vritra was standing in the middle of the hall, completely surrounded by all the assassins.
"W- What? He is so... cough..." The same assassin stared at the empty space in front of him in shock. But suddenly, his vision began to shift.
Then blood began dripping from his belly; under the shocked gazes of all the assassins, the near level 400 assassin was cut in two—without any of them noticing it.
THUD
The upper half of his body fell to the ground, while his lower half remained standing for a few seconds as if unaware of his own death before finally falling forward.
[Sin Point Gained: Shocked +602]
[Sin Point Gained: Frightened +533]
Vritra’s smile stretched wide. He truly looked like a devil.
With the Myriad level armor and Myriad soul wraith protecting him at all times, Vritra had absolutely nothing to worry about—even if he just stood there letting them all attack.
Raising his axes, he rotated them so that the hammer part came in front. After all, it wouldn’t be good to just kill them all with a single strike.
ROOOAAAAAARRRRRRRRRRRRRR
Vritra let out an ear piercing dragon roar that made dozens of assassins bleed. His roar resounded for several kilometers and frightened everyone.
It was the roar of a real dragon.
Everything remained still for a moment before chaos erupted.
Despite being frightened, the assassins charged at Vritra—holding all kinds of weapons, many even trying to sneak attack or hit him with secret weapons.
On the other hand, Vritra completely disregarded self defense as he began to swing the axes around wildly.
BANG!!
The bodies of a dozen assassins exploded the moment they were hit by the explosive force, their bodies creating a blood mist in the air.
Even if the hammers slightly grazed against their bodies, the assassins were left with broken limbs or severe wounds.
"C- Charge forward, we have to hold him here until our leader arrives! As soon as he gets here, this intruder will be dealt with so—" one of the men was shouting from the back of the crowd.
But his body shivered as Vritra disappeared from everyone’s vision, then a chilling voice sounded in his ear.
"Surprise!!"
BOOOOOM!!

His body was enveloped by a shadow. As he glanced up, he was only able to see the enormous surface of the hammer. Before he could even let out a painful cry, one of the heavy hammers slammed into his body.
His bones were crushed, his flesh and organs turned into minced meat; as Vritra pulled his hammer back, there was only a red sticky mess on the floor.
By now, there were more than seven hundred assassins in the large hall. Vritra glanced at them with a twisted smile, his entire being seeming to have changed at this moment.
Dozens of hidden attacks were launched toward him, but before they could even come into contact with his skin, all the attacks were blocked.
His body was already drenched in blood. The Myriad armor didn’t stop the blood since it wasn’t harmful.
Vritra stretched both his hands to his sides, separating the two weapons.
BOOOOOOOOOOM!!
Then using all his strength, he brought the two to the front as the hammers struck one another. A destructive wave was released with a deafening explosion.

All the people in front of him were thrown several meters back, their hearts thumping wildly. Just this shockwave was enough to make more than half of the assassins cough out blood. They had finally understood how pitifully weak they actually were in front of this demon.
Their first instinct was to run. But the moment they turned around... all these assassins noticed that they were trapped in a dust dune, where people were able to enter but not leave.
Controlling the dust, Vritra scanned the entire hall. Then with precision, he sent dust swarming into the bodies of all the assassins present.
No matter what they tried, most of the assassins couldn’t stop such an attack. They tried to cover their ears and noses, but the dust would just tear their skin and enter.
The assassins couldn’t understand what was happening at first, but then an unimaginable amount of pain shot through their bodies, making them fall to the ground instantly.

The dust took forms of tiny devils in their bodies and wreaked havoc. They tore their flesh, cut the bones into tiny pieces, made a mess of internal organs. Popped eyes, cut veins—it was a total mess. Those tiny dust demons just destroyed whatever was around them.
Painful wails instantly resounded across the entire hall. Only a very few assassins were able to stop the dust from entering their bodies... less than five.

More than eight hundred assassins were rolling on the ground and screaming wildly. The lucky ones were those whose brains were targeted first; they only felt a single wave of pain, as those devils crawled into their brains and cut them apart.
They were killed only after a few seconds, but only a few were lucky enough to have their brains destroyed first.
"No more! Ahhhhhh my skin, uwaaaaah it’s peeling! Guhh COUGH COUGH, kill me—Kill me already, you demon!!"

"Sob... I d- didn’t do anything... p- please... oh god—my eyes!! It hurts so much, ughhhh COUGH COUGH COUGH!" another man screamed before coughing out several mouthfuls of blood and spatting out his tongue.
"W- Why me?! AHHHHH my legs are g- gone! Cough—ghkkk So painful! Ughh—get it out! S- Something’s—in me! It’s moving—AAHHH!!"
Painful and heart wrenching screams rang out all over the place. It was complete hell. Limbs and organs were lying all over the place, blood pools formed on the ground.
It was dozens of times more brutal than the deaths of all those Nine Pacts’ men. What Vritra was giving wasn’t just death—but suffering... pain to the extreme level.
The tiny devils, that looked as if they were made of metal, began ripping apart their nerves—making them feel all kinds of pain. Just breathing became a very agonizing task for them soon.

chapters.title: Chapter 121: Brutality
paragraphs: Vritra looked around at all the assassins that were already on the ground. Striking them now would be showing them mercy. So he ignored them all and fixed his gaze on the four assassins that were still left standing.
All four of them were above level 600, with the highest being at 655. Vritra’s own level was at 628—if seen normally, then there should be a huge power difference between the two.
Well, there was a big power difference, but not in the way most would assume.
The four assassins were the strongest leaders of the Dawn Minion group—they were only under the leader. There was one more, but he had gone out on a mission.
Even the four assassins were terrified by the sight in front of them. They wondered what kind of monster their organization had offended to be reduced to this state within minutes.
"Who exactly are you? And what is your reason for causing trouble here?" one of them asked. He just wanted to buy some time; of course, Vritra’s reason to kill an assassin organization was obvious.
"..." Vritra looked at the four men before fixing his gaze on the man who had just asked the question. He pointed one of the axes towards him and said:
"Got you!!"
In the next instant, Vritra—along with the weapons he was holding—crumbled into dust, shocking all four of the men.
It was just a clone.
The strongest assassin among them felt slight rustling of air behind him. Without even saying anything, he swung his blade behind his back with all his might while jumping away.
WHOOSH
The blade tore through a body, cutting it in half. But the first assassin was shocked to see that it wasn’t Vritra who had just died—it was one of the assassins who was already suffering.
"Where is he? I can’t sense his presence at all. Is he an assassin too? What kind of technique is this?" the second one spoke, looking around vigilantly; his body continued to tremble.

The entire hall was filled with a palpable tension. There was little to no chance of survival. The horrifying screams made the situation much worse—the four assassins understood that Vritra was a psycho.

Even if their work involved killing, most of them didn’t enjoy the task and just did it because they had to. But Vritra—he was enjoying the entire act. He seemed more excited the more the people screamed in pain.

"Get closer," the first assassin suggested as the four stood close to one another, with their backs pressed together. This way they were able to look in all directions and had a higher chance of defending against any surprise attack.
Vritra’s voice sounded suddenly.
"Forbid: Mana!!"
[Forbidden Activated.]

He appeared in front of the fourth assassin, who had a terrified look on his face but still tried to launch an attack—only to notice the next moment that he couldn’t access any of the mana in his body.
"H-How is this possib—Ughhh!" He hastily pushed his blade forward, but Vritra casually waved one of the axes, cutting off both his feet near the knees.
The scream of the fourth assassin sounded as he fell down. The other three were alerted and attacked Vritra at the same time.
"Forbid: Vision!!"
[Forbidden Activated.]

Vritra’s casual voice sounded as his body turned into dust and disappeared. At the same time, the second assassin’s vision went dark. He was startled and so frightened that he began to swing his blades around randomly.
"Uwaaaah I CAN’T SEE ANYTHING!! AHHHHHH M-MY EYES—"
The other two assassins easily dodged his blades, but the fourth assassin—whose body was falling to the ground—couldn’t.
The blade slashed at his eyes, cutting them both in half. Finding a target, the second man didn’t stop as he madly cut at the head of the fourth assassin.
His cheeks were torn, his jaw was cut into several parts, his nose fell off, even his neck was almost torn apart.
"Forbid: Strength."
[Forbidden Activated.]
Vritra mumbled. The number two’s vision finally returned, and he saw the terrifying scene of his blade plunged deep into the skull of his friend.
He was horrified and fell back, his body shivering badly. He vomited and began to run away.

The number three, who was holding two metallic knives, suddenly felt extremely weak—just standing became an impossible chore for him. The two knives fell from his hands as if their weight had increased by dozens of times in an instant.
At that moment, an axe descended from the top.
BANGGG
The sharp blade struck exactly the third assassin’s head, then it continued to move down, slicing his body in two vertically.
The axe passed through his flesh and organs as if cutting through empty air. The third man had a dreadful expression on his face, his eyes filled with regret and questions.
Then the two parts fell in opposite directions, as the blood and organs flowed out like a mess.
The second assassin saw this and became even more terrified.

"You bastard, fight me head-on if you dare!" the first assassin roared with bloodshot eyes. Even as assassins, they had little relationship with each other, but they could still be considered one large family.
And now every single one of them was dying such pitiful deaths, without even knowing why they were being killed.
[Nether Eye Activated.]

Vritra’s figure appeared in front of the first assassin, who had gone mad with bloodlust. But his body paused as he saw the vertical eye on Vritra’s forehead containing endless darkness. For some reason, he felt a strong danger from it.
An invisible wave of energy shot out of the Nether Eye and struck the first assassin, who had no way to defend against it.
But Vritra didn’t pause...
He spent even more mental energy, sending one more mental attack.
Then again...
And again...
The first man’s weapons fell to the ground as he clutched his head tightly and fell to his knees.

His scream reverberated across the hall—none of his words were understandable. His hair turned white extremely fast before withering away. Then the first assassin’s skin began to shrink as blood seeped out of all the pores on his body.
Receiving several devastating mental attacks completely wrecked his body, inside and out.
His eyes bulged to an impossible length before popping out of the sockets and hanging by the nerves connecting them, giving a bloody view of his skull. The sight was extremely gruesome.
Vritra no longer paid any attention to him and looked at the second assassin, who was trying to wriggle his way out of the dust dune.
Vritra felt a headache since a large amount of his mental energy was exhausted, but with his passive skills working in the background along with Shift, it began to recover rapidly.
"Where is your leader?" Vritra moved and flashed in front of the man, who already seemed to have gone crazy.

"I-I don’t know sob sob uwaaaah p-please spare me, I d-don’t even know you... sob sob I hadn’t done a-anything... I have a family... please, I am working to feed t-them... sob sob... I don’t want to die..." the second man cried and begged.

chapters.title: Chapter 122: Dawn
paragraphs: Vritra frowned as he heard the second man’s begging.
After a moment, he muttered: "Bobby."
The metallic ball flashed and pierced through the assassin’s brain, killing him instantly.
All four of the strongest present were dead.
Vritra turned and looked at the few people who were still wriggling and groaning on the ground.
"Go ahead," he ordered, and instantly Hellmancer began to collect the souls of all the fallen assassins and killed if they still had some vitality left.
He looked away from the soul wraith, who was happily picking up the souls like free money, and turned his gaze towards the direction of the stairs.
Within a minute, a little over nine hundred men had already died.
A few more people kept entering the dome—only to regret their decision as they were instantly attacked by the tiny dust devils.
Outside the black market, a black ray of light flashed at an extreme speed, heading straight towards the base of the Dawn Minion.
Wherever he ran, he left behind an extreme murderous aura, making the surrounding seem as if a disaster had just passed.
It was Dawn, the leader of the Dawn Minion—the one person who could match the battle strength of the Golden Knight, the hidden protector of the king.

He had travelled far because of a mission he had received from the Nine Pacts. They wanted him to create some trouble near one of the borders, kill a few guards, and turn the arrangements there upside down.
He ran back the moment he had received that danger signal, but just after a few seconds, the life spheres of all the members of his Dawn Minion began to explode at an extremely fast speed.
Even four of the five sub leaders were killed in such a short span, and more than ninety percent of the members were already dead.
All his life’s work— everything he had put so much effort into— was being destroyed just like that.
He felt enraged— so much that he disregarded everything and used one of his trump cards to arrive at his home as soon as possible. Yet he was still too late.
Not a single member of his large family was left by the time he arrived there.
Taking out a short sword, the streak of light entered the black market and then headed straight for the place where all his people were being killed.
WHOOSH
Right after entering, the first thing he saw were the hundreds of corpses—all dismembered and in pieces. They weren’t even given a simple death; all of them were tortured before they were killed.
Dawn’s rage shot off the roof as he let out a wild roar and, with his short sword, charged toward the only person still standing amongst the layer of corpses.
Using his speed, Dawn made his move before that merciless killer could notice and plunged his sword through his chest, pinning him against the wall.
"DIE, YOU IMBECILE!!! DIEEEEEEE!!" While staring at his blood stained face, Dawn roared.
But despite being stabbed right into the heart, this murderer didn’t show any sign of fear or pain. Instead, his twisted smile widened as his body began to deform.
"Looking for me?" A mocking voice sounded right beside the leader, surprising him a bit, since the one he had killed was just a dust clone.
But he quickly came back to his senses, wasting no time.
He moved at full speed and rotated around while waving the short sword, drawing a half circle in the air.
WHOOSH
CLANG
But as the sword hit Vritra’s shoulder, he was only pushed back one step. It wasn’t able to harm him in the slightest.
"Is that all?" Vritra’s smile cracked as he looked at the leader with a crazy expression. This was the person who had targeted his mother in his absence.
"..." Dawn didn’t want to talk at all. He instantly began to use his strongest move as black smoke began to gather around his short sword.
But just then, the enraged leader saw a metallic ball the size of a fist flash in front of his eyes, and at a terrifying speed, the ball cut off both his hands from around his wrists.

The move was interrupted, and the vast amount of energy had no place to escape. All of this was too sudden, and Dawn wasn’t able to control anything as both his hands exploded violently into a bloody mess.
BOOOOOOM!!

He was thrown back and smashed into the wall, coughing blood as the entire hall shook violently. Pain and shock were written all over his face. Since he was on an open mission, he didn’t even have the time to cover his face.
"M- Myriad level?!!" As one of the strongest people in the entire Dunshire Kingdom, of course he knew about them—though he had never seen one before.
’So powerful, no wonder... so we never stood a chance against him from the start. Sigh... Just why is this all happening?

Being from a murderous occupation, we all know that we would never have a good end, but this... did we end up between the conspiracies of top powers?’ Dawn coughed violently and stared at Vritra in a daze.
After a moment, it seemed he had given up on fighting. He simply asked: "J- Just why did you haa do all this?"
Vritra walked closer to him and instead of answering, he asked a question of his own: "A couple days ago, someone asked your assassin group to abduct a woman from the castle. Who was it?"
"..." Dawn fell into deep thoughts.
He had been out for the important missions of the Nine Pacts, so his underlings had been looking over all the missions. But he was aware of all the missions they took.
"COUGH I- It was one of the leaders of the Nine Pacts— t- the group of low tier leaders sent to this place from that d- dark organisation." Dawn answered honestly.
There was no point in lying now.
He wanted the people responsible for the end of the Dawn Minion to suffer as well.
Either the Nine Pacts would suffer, or Vritra and his backer would end up dying. At least that would put the souls of all the assassins to peace.
"...I see." Vritra nodded and regretted giving those people from the Nine Pacts fast deaths.
Then he turned and disappeared. The metallic ball flashed again and killed Dawn before Hellmancer picked his soul—and even the sword.
From that day on, there would no longer be any Dawn Minion.
Vritra flew out of the black market and headed straight to meet with Dark Knight at the entrance of the forest.
He felt a bit better after slaughtering the Dawn Minion, but killing people still left a bitter taste behind.
But he would do it again and again if someone tried to harm someone he loved.
It wasn’t long before he arrived at his destination. Dark Knight stood there with a little over fifty men, all of them tied together by a black chain that left them immobile.
As soon as Vritra landed, Dark Knight bowed and spoke: "Master, I have gathered all the men who allowed those assassins to enter last night."
After a pause, he continued...

chapters.title: Chapter 123: Puppets
paragraphs: "Along with those guards, I have even gathered the guards that had gone along with your group to the labyrinth, except for the guard commander," Dark Knight reported.
Vritra nodded. He was no longer in any mood to kill all these personally. So after looking over all the men, he brought out the Chimera and Hellmancer, then ordered:

"Kill all these men, and after you are done absorbing their souls, head directly to the labyrinth and to the lowest floor. Then start your training there. None of you can return until you have at least become Myriad Soul Wraiths."
Normally, if they fought for too long, their energies would be exhausted, but when killing so many demons, they would be easily able to replenish their energies from the souls.
Yasmine could control that trap even from afar, so as soon as these people entered, they would be bombarded with the strongest demons—and countless of them.
Levelling up from the soul of the Demon Lord was the best way for them to grow for now. Not to mention, Vritra would also be gaining levels at the same time.
"We understand, master," Dark Knight replied for the group of three.
After giving a few more instructions to the Soul Wraiths, Vritra turned around and flew away, completely ignoring the pleas of those guards.
A kingdom suffers when ruled by a rotten crown.
This was exactly what those lines meant—colluding with the Nine Pacts, the king had dug his own grave.
While Vritra was on the topic of revenge, he decided to settle one more score—with the commander of guards that had acted all high and mighty in the labyrinth.

He would never be able to forget that scene, that feeling of helplessness when he was forced into that death canopy. Vritra didn’t want to just inflict physical pain upon that commander; that would be too small. He needed to suffer more.

Hellmancer had followed that commander for a short time and had delivered most of the information about him to Vritra. The commander lived not far away from the castle boundary. By doing all the shady things, he had acquired quite a bit of fortune.
He had a happy family—a wife and two little kids.
Vritra headed directly towards the house of the commander, who should be at his home today.
After a few minutes, Vritra landed in front of a luxurious house. It was quite large and built in a spacious area with a big lawn outside.
Vritra walked towards the door and stopped in front of the guards standing there. He wore a mask on his face to hide his identity since he planned to stay in this kingdom for a few more days.
"Call the commander outside. I have some important orders to deliver to him," Vritra said, and to not waste time, he showed a seal of the king that he had borrowed from the goddess previously.
"O-Oh, yes sir, please give us a moment." One of the two guards nodded hastily and ran into the house.

It didn’t take long for the commander to come running out after hearing that someone had brought orders from the king himself. He was surprised to see the masked person there. The commander didn’t remember seeing someone like that before, but the royal seal was real, so he gestured for Vritra to enter.
"This place is fine to talk. This matter is of utter importance, so you shouldn’t share this with anyone else," Vritra said as he put away the royal seal.
"Yes, I understand. Please tell me what is it the king wants me to do," the commander spoke respectfully.
Vritra scanned the entire house with his senses and saw a woman playing with her children and a total of five servants working there.
He controlled dust, and suddenly all of them found themselves trapped in dust cocoons; they tried to break it but couldn’t—even their screams couldn’t leak out of it.
All the cocoons flew out of the house from behind, without anyone noticing.
After this was done, Vritra removed his mask and, with a smile, he spoke, "Long time no see, commander."
"!!!" The middle-aged man was shocked as he staggered backwards. How could he not remember that face even if it had changed quite a bit?
"Y-You... what are you doing here?" the commander asked in shock. He glanced back at his house and felt an inexplicable fear.
"We had a debt to settle between us, and I just came to get even with you," Vritra said as he wore back his mask and stood there calmly.
"Do you think you have the strength to threaten me?" the commander said with an icy expression, while internally he was panicking. He understood that everything Vritra had said before was just a lie.
"Of course. But you are not my target." Vritra raised his right hand, and suddenly the surroundings darkened slightly—almost as if the sun had started to set or it was covered by clouds.
The commander raised his head, only to see an enormous dark metallic ball that was at least as big as his house. It hovered in the air right above their heads.
"W-What are you talking abou—?" The commander was truly terrified. He felt that what he was fearing the most was about to come true.

Vritra waved his hand as the ball began to descend upon the house. Its speed was so fast that by the time the commander registered the changes, Bobby had crashed into the house, turning it into a complete mess.
"Nooooooooo!!" The commander screamed in horror. His wife, his children—they were still inside that house. But now...
Everything was gone in a moment. There was no way they would survive something like that. He fell to his knees as tears streaked down his cheeks. His soul itself seemed to have been pierced.
"So, commander, do you like my present?" Vritra asked, looking at the commander with an emotionless face.

"Y-You monster, how could you? M-My family... sob sob... how can you be so heartless? You bastard, how could you kill innocent children for sob... something they don’t even know about. You should have sob sob killed me.
H-How can this be... J-Joey... cough... I-I am sorry. It’s all my fault... my kids..." the commander rang like a broken record. He cried and sobbed for a few seconds.
The explosion had attracted a lot of attention. Although Bobby had already vanished, lots of people began to run into the lawn.
The commander pulled out a knife from his shoe, and in the next second, he stabbed it into his chest. He didn’t suffer much physically, yet he looked the most broken of them all.

Vritra vanished from there. He was done with killing most of his targets, but his mood was still quite bad. Of course, he wouldn’t kill those innocent people—they had just been moved behind the house.
As he flew back towards the temple, Vritra thought about puppets.
Greedy puppets, helpless puppets, weak puppets, strong puppets...

Controlled by strings and doing whatever the hands above them made them do—that’s how weak people live. None of them have any will of their own. Even someone powerful who is not truly powerful could be controlled by those puppet masters.
And Vritra would never want to be a puppet.

chapters.title: Chapter 124: A pig
paragraphs: Within a few minutes, Vritra arrived back at the temple. Since his entire body was covered in blood, he stepped out of the fourth dimension straight into his bathroom.

Vanessa was sitting on the bed and reading a book. She loved reading, and this new world had a whole new collection for her. When she heard the sound of water, she was surprised at first but soon relaxed upon sensing that it was Vritra.
"Honey, are you alright?" she called out, wondering how and why he went directly into the bathroom.
"Yes, I am fine, mom," Vritra replied as he removed the scent of blood from his body completely and threw the dirty clothes into his inventory.
Soon, he walked out of there completely refreshed. He stopped in front of his mother and just slumped down into her lap, hugging her waist tightly while his head rested over her thigh.
Vanessa caressed his head lovingly, as she set aside the book and asked again, "Are you really alright?"
"...Yes, I am fine, just a bit tired. Let me get a nap," Vritra replied. He closed his eyes and felt his body relax, feeling her warmth.
"Sure, don’t worry about a thing and rest," she whispered and continued to move her fingers through his long, smooth hair.
Vritra slept for a couple of hours. The nap really refreshed his mind; Vanessa’s presence was especially relaxing.
After waking up, Vanessa began to prepare lunch for the both of them, while Vritra sat alone at the dining table, deep in his own thoughts.

’Now I want a bit of peaceful time. Just training with mom, taming Diana, saving Fiona, and of course talking with my naughty wifey,’ he thought. He had taken too many lives in just a span of two days.

First the Nine Pacts, then the Dawn Minion, and those guards. Even if all of them deserved to die for what they had done, it still left a strange feeling behind. But Vritra knew he would have to kill much more in the future, so he allowed himself to completely drown in and get used to such feelings.
"And the food is ready." Vanessa smiled and set the food for Vritra before taking her seat. Then she rested her chin over her hands and asked, "Eat and tell me how it tastes."
"..." Vritra nodded and tested all the dishes. As his taste buds exploded, he answered while eating, "Mom, this is great. Just perfect."

"Haha, eat slowly." Vanessa giggled as she watched him eat everything. After a moment, she asked, "I have always been curious about something. How did you get the goddess to help you? She was so haughty before, but now she is... well, like a well-behaved puppy."
"GULP. Well, somehow I was able to have control over her life and death, so she has no choice but to obey me," Vritra answered without stopping.

"Oh, hehe, that’s good. I hated how she talked to you when we arrived here and wanted to give her a few hard slaps. Make sure you tame her good. She still seems a bit rebellious," Vanessa said with an evil smile.
"Hmm yes, I will, mom. Soon you’ll have to go with her to another kingdom, and I’ll follow behind you separately," Vritra reminded her, and Vanessa nodded.
The two talked for a while longer, then they took a walk around the temple together, spending some wholesome time while just talking without a worry about anything.

Vanessa went back to the temple after that while Vritra decided to pay a visit to the training area, to meet his good friend Max. After a thought, he sent Bobby to finish off all the people remaining from the Nine Pacts in their hideout—mostly the doctors were left now.
Most of their victims were in very bad states and had no chance of survival, after being injected with unknown fluids or being torn apart to have other creatures’ limbs added to their bodies.
Bobby had easily killed those weak doctors, and after the huge commotion, the Golden Moon arrived there to rescue the victims.
As Vritra had expected, the act of him killing all those members of the Nine Pacts had caused a big commotion. Although they were just low-level members, they were still part of the organization.

Not to mention, their experiments were interrupted and a huge treasure was stolen from right under their noses. The Golden Moon had suffered a loss in the Divine Tomb too, but almost all their members were fine, so they didn’t put much effort into finding that person.

But the Nine Pacts were different. The Dunshire Kingdom had successfully captured their attention. However, since the danger was low, they decided to take care of that person with a single team—a team capable enough to bring the entire kingdom to ruins.
After a few days of receiving the news, the team left to finish the mission.

Nearly thirty of the teenagers were fighting against demons, completely unaware of all the chaos that had occurred outside of the kingdom. Fiona had just killed one orc. She sat to the side and decided to take some rest, her body wet from sweat and her clothes stuck to her body.
She looked as Max used his fast speed to deliver fatal strikes to the demon he was fighting. His electric ability gave his agility a huge boost.

After killing the demon, he looked at her and said in an arrogant tone, "You got tired just after killing a few demons? Hah, are you going to rest like that on the battlefield while those demons wait for the queen to complete her rest?"
Fiona frowned. Her trembling lips parted as she tried to speak, "I was just..."

"Tch, how are you going to grow like that? Hmph, weak." After speaking haughtily, he went to fight another demon, thinking, ’This is what you like, right? Bad boys, bad treatment, red flags? Sigh... I don’t like treating her like this, but she’s the type who enjoys rude behavior.’
Max glanced back secretly, feeling bad that he was speaking to her like this. He really loved her a lot and decided to stop acting like this soon—he couldn’t bear to treat her like this.
Fiona: "..."
She couldn’t believe this was the same Max. Even though he had been a jerk to others, he had always been so gentle to her, but now...

"Tch tch. What a pig, how can he treat an innocent and cute girl like that? Sigh, I really don’t understand what made you fall for him." Suddenly, a strangely familiar voice sounded just beside her ear.
Fiona was surprised as she turned her head and saw that same handsome face. She was frozen with shock once again. He was sitting right beside her, yet she didn’t even notice.
Vritra casually took her right hand and looked at the tiny wound she had gotten while fighting the orcs. He blew on it and caressed her tender skin.
A warm sensation spread through her hand as the wound healed instantly, and the slight pain disappeared along with it.
Fiona pulled her hand away hastily and glanced over at Max. Thankfully, he was busy fighting the demon, so he didn’t notice their intimate gesture just now.

sentences.text: Within a few minutes, Vritra arrived back at the temple.
Since his entire body was covered in blood, he stepped out of the fourth dimension straight into his bathroom.
Vanessa was sitting on the bed and reading a book.
She loved reading, and this new world had a whole new collection for her.
When she heard the sound of water, she was surprised at first but soon relaxed upon sensing that it was Vritra.
"Honey, are you alright?" she called out, wondering how and why he went directly into the bathroom.
"Yes, I am fine, mom," Vritra replied as he removed the scent of blood from his body completely and threw the dirty clothes into his inventory.
Soon, he walked out of there completely refreshed.
He stopped in front of his mother and just slumped down into her lap, hugging her waist tightly while his head rested over her thigh.
Vanessa caressed his head lovingly, as she set aside the book and asked again, "Are you really alright?"
"...Yes, I am fine, just a bit tired.
Let me get a nap," Vritra replied.
He closed his eyes and felt his body relax, feeling her warmth.
"Sure, don’t worry about a thing and rest," she whispered and continued to move her fingers through his long, smooth hair.
Vritra slept for a couple of hours.
The nap really refreshed his mind; Vanessa’s presence was especially relaxing.
After waking up, Vanessa began to prepare lunch for the both of them, while Vritra sat alone at the dining table, deep in his own thoughts.
’Now I want a bit of peaceful time.
Just training with mom, taming Diana, saving Fiona, and of course talking with my naughty wifey,’ he thought.
He had taken too many lives in just a span of two days.
First the Nine Pacts, then the Dawn Minion, and those guards.
Even if all of them deserved to die for what they had done, it still left a strange feeling behind.
But Vritra knew he would have to kill much more in the future, so he allowed himself to completely drown in and get used to such feelings.
"And the food is ready." Vanessa smiled and set the food for Vritra before taking her seat.
Then she rested her chin over her hands and asked, "Eat and tell me how it tastes."
"..." Vritra nodded and tested all the dishes.
As his taste buds exploded, he answered while eating, "Mom, this is great.
Just perfect."
"Haha, eat slowly." Vanessa giggled as she watched him eat everything.
After a moment, she asked, "I have always been curious about something.
How did you get the goddess to help you?
She was so haughty before, but now she is... well, like a well-behaved puppy."
"GULP.
Well, somehow I was able to have control over her life and death, so she has no choice but to obey me," Vritra answered without stopping.
"Oh, hehe, that’s good.
I hated how she talked to you when we arrived here and wanted to give her a few hard slaps.
Make sure you tame her good.
She still seems a bit rebellious," Vanessa said with an evil smile.
"Hmm yes, I will, mom.
Soon you’ll have to go with her to another kingdom, and I’ll follow behind you separately," Vritra reminded her, and Vanessa nodded.
The two talked for a while longer, then they took a walk around the temple together, spending some wholesome time while just talking without a worry about anything.
Vanessa went back to the temple after that while Vritra decided to pay a visit to the training area, to meet his good friend Max.
After a thought, he sent Bobby to finish off all the people remaining from the Nine Pacts in their hideout—mostly the doctors were left now.
Most of their victims were in very bad states and had no chance of survival, after being injected with unknown fluids or being torn apart to have other creatures’ limbs added to their bodies.
Bobby had easily killed those weak doctors, and after the huge commotion, the Golden Moon arrived there to rescue the victims.
As Vritra had expected, the act of him killing all those members of the Nine Pacts had caused a big commotion.
Although they were just low-level members, they were still part of the organization.
Not to mention, their experiments were interrupted and a huge treasure was stolen from right under their noses.
The Golden Moon had suffered a loss in the Divine Tomb too, but almost all their members were fine, so they didn’t put much effort into finding that person.
But the Nine Pacts were different.
The Dunshire Kingdom had successfully captured their attention.
However, since the danger was low, they decided to take care of that person with a single team—a team capable enough to bring the entire kingdom to ruins.
After a few days of receiving the news, the team left to finish the mission.
Nearly thirty of the teenagers were fighting against demons, completely unaware of all the chaos that had occurred outside of the kingdom.
Fiona had just killed one orc.
She sat to the side and decided to take some rest, her body wet from sweat and her clothes stuck to her body.
She looked as Max used his fast speed to deliver fatal strikes to the demon he was fighting.
His electric ability gave his agility a huge boost.
After killing the demon, he looked at her and said in an arrogant tone, "You got tired just after killing a few demons?
Hah, are you going to rest like that on the battlefield while those demons wait for the queen to complete her rest?"
Fiona frowned.
Her trembling lips parted as she tried to speak, "I was just..."
"Tch, how are you going to grow like that?
Hmph, weak." After speaking haughtily, he went to fight another demon, thinking, ’This is what you like, right?
Bad boys, bad treatment, red flags?
Sigh...
I don’t like treating her like this, but she’s the type who enjoys rude behavior.’
Max glanced back secretly, feeling bad that he was speaking to her like this.
He really loved her a lot and decided to stop acting like this soon—he couldn’t bear to treat her like this.
Fiona: "..."
She couldn’t believe this was the same Max.
Even though he had been a jerk to others, he had always been so gentle to her, but now...
"Tch tch.
What a pig, how can he treat an innocent and cute girl like that?
Sigh, I really don’t understand what made you fall for him." Suddenly, a strangely familiar voice sounded just beside her ear.
Fiona was surprised as she turned her head and saw that same handsome face.
She was frozen with shock once again.
He was sitting right beside her, yet she didn’t even notice.
Vritra casually took her right hand and looked at the tiny wound she had gotten while fighting the orcs.
He blew on it and caressed her tender skin.
A warm sensation spread through her hand as the wound healed instantly, and the slight pain disappeared along with it.
Fiona pulled her hand away hastily and glanced over at Max.
Thankfully, he was busy fighting the demon, so he didn’t notice their intimate gesture just now.

chapters.title: Chapter 125: Again? Just Throw me away directly, why dont you?
paragraphs: Vritra sat on the ground beside Fiona, while on his left his only friend—Zengis—was sitting along with one of its two new friends, Bob.
The stone with a face on it attracted a few gazes, but no one paid it too much attention, while Bob looked just like a metallic ball—no one paid it any attention.
Fiona heaved a sigh of relief upon seeing that Max hadn’t seen Vritra hold her hand, then she looked down and saw that the small cut had disappeared from her milky skin.
After Vritra’s healing skill had increased in level, he could even use it on others to heal, though the effects weren’t as great.
Though reluctant, she still decided to thank him.
"...Thank you—wait, what are you doing here? And when did you arrive?" she asked. The more they met, the more mysterious he seemed.
"I came to meet you, of course. And I arrived here when Max was shouting at you. His love language sure is strange," Vritra said with a chuckle.

Looking around at his classmates, he realized how peaceful their lives had been so far compared to his own. They were killing the captured demons in such a safe environment. At most, they would only receive minor injuries—there was absolutely no danger to their lives.
{Sin Point Gained: Surprised +1}
"Meet me? Why?" Fiona asked, glancing back at Max, who was running around and busy fighting an orc.
"Hmm, did you forget or are you just pretending?" Vritra shook his head and then added, "Did you forget we had a deal? The special game? Does any of it ring a bell?"
{Sin Point Gained: Baffled +1}

"Ah... that’s—" Fiona suddenly remembered. The ecchi game. Her cheeks instantly reddened slightly. A part of her—the part that is twisted, curious, and horny—really wanted to see what this ecchi game of his was going to be.
But the other part, which was still loyal to Max, made her feel ashamed and guilty for even having that thought. How could she ever betray Max?
"What are the two of you talking about?" Just then, an enraged voice sounded.
{Sin Point Gained: Enraged +1}
Both Vritra and Fiona looked up and saw Max, who was slightly dirty with blood of the orcs, walking towards them with a deep frown on his face.
Fiona tried to hide her face, which was blushing heavily, and Vritra remained casual, not caring about his existence.
Max felt so angry that he just wanted to cut Vritra to pieces. He was always lingering around Fiona, even though she was already in love with Max.

"Ah... he just arrived here, h-he was just telling me about uhm..." Fiona panicked and didn’t know what to say. Their relationship was already turning so bad, she didn’t want Max to misunderstand anything.
"I was just confessing my love to her, actually," Vritra said, shrugging his shoulders.
"Y-Yes, he was confessing his love—huh?" Fiona just repeated his words, only to be surprised by it. Won’t these words just increase the misunderstanding? She was even blushing!!
{Sin Point Gained: Shocked +1}

"... " Max clenched his fists so tight that his knuckles turned white, his nails cutting the skin of his own palm. It was exactly as he thought—that ugly Vritra really was here to steal his lover. How could he allow such a thing to happen?
{Sin Point Gained: Cursed +1}
{Sin Point Gained: Ridiculed +1}
"You janitor, stay away from her... if you don’t want to get beaten up—" Max glared at Vritra and threatened but was interrupted by Vritra, who laughed and asked:
"Beaten like last time? Damn, you are too scary, sir. Do you plan to kill me by tickling with those cute electric shocks?"
{Sin Point Gained: Dazed +1}
"Hah, you dodging monkey! Had you not been dodging all over the place, then you would already be toast." Max retorted, his face burning with humiliation.
"Oh my god, I didn’t know this is how the game is played. So I needed to stand still and get hit by your attack? How silly of me. I understand now.

Sir Max, you’re clearly destined for greatness... I can already see it: demons lining up, patiently waiting their turn to get poked by your mighty thunder tickle!" Vritra said and clapped his fist into his palm with exaggerated realization.
{Sin Point Gained: Speechless +1}

"You!! Shut up! You can merely move the dust and clean the floors. I don’t need to hear that from someone like you!" Max shouted. He didn’t want to admit it, but even he knew that Vritra was somehow a tiny bit stronger than him.
"Fiona, let’s go." Max glared at Vritra and then extended his right hand towards Fiona. He could keep his red flag act for later, but not now.
[Natural Hypnosis Activated.]
Fiona smiled.
Seeing him act like that, she felt that he still was in love with her—it made her happier. She nodded and was about to take his hand when she remembered something...

Jace and Tyler’s words—and a disgust rose from within her body. Even if she felt it was all false, her outstretched hand retracted in haste, leaving Max standing there with his right hand extended towards her with a shocked expression.
Seeing his face, Fiona instantly regretted doing that.
"Ah—I was... I was going to kill more demons." Fiona stood up on her own and dusted her clothes, cursing herself for believing in the nonsense for even a moment.
"Alright, let’s hunt together." Max pulled his hand back and nodded with his old kind smile, before glaring at Vritra again and turning away to leave.

"Haha. Are you just going to walk away again? Too scared of me, electro boy?" Vritra’s mocking tone made Max’s feet halt. A boy in love—or any normal boy—tends to act stupid and angry when they are insulted in front of a girl, especially if it’s someone they love.
{Sin Point Gained: Snapped +1}
Max’s face turned red and his body shook in anger. He wanted to tear apart that hateful face and then strangle him to death.
"Fine, tell me what is it you want? Do you want to fight again?" Max glanced at Fiona, and seeing that she had also heard Vritra, he couldn’t stop himself from acting tough.
’Ughh... Not again...’ Fiona felt a headache.

The previous price hadn’t been paid yet and her stupid lover was about to start it all over again. She wondered if he wanted to push her to Vritra that badly. Why don’t you just throw me at him directly.
Why was he so stupid? Can’t he see how powerful and smart Vritra is?
How could the difference between max and Vritra be so huge.
{Sin Point Gained: Praised +1}
He could easily manipulate this blockhead.

"Hmm. How about we keep things simple this time? Instead of a fight, how about arm wrestling?" Vritra said and stood up, his eyes holding a mocking look that irked Max even more. He put Zengis back into inventory and Bob silently disappeared into his shadow.
{Sin Point Gained: Got Taunted +1}

"Good, good. You won’t be able to jump around like a darn monkey that way." Max grinned. He was quite confident in his physical strength—that’s the place where he had been putting most of his free points, after all.
